cases.oracle: The guest setup compiles a deterministic two-thread fixture and runs parser controls plus a native sibling ptrace control, including complete syscall returns and natural thread exits. For each case, setup starts the actual candidate shell blocked on stdin and a separate owned tracee, verifies live distinct tasks, ownership, untraced state and closed shared-memory gates, then invokes -p on that same tracee. It samples per-TID TracerPid in both task orders before release, releases worker then leader only after worker exit, and records actual fixture and candidate status, timeout and raw stdout/stderr. Failed infrastructure checks fail setup; a valid completed fixture with a candidate mismatch is retained for candidate assessment. PR_SET_PTRACER authorizes only the candidate PID. The primary approved native oracle substitution is conditional on reviewed guest evidence and does not claim GNU strace equivalence.
cases.purpose: Attach to an already-running owned process and trace until it exits naturally.
cases.comparison: Require the controlled invocation to have a complete setup record and native control, then a complete line-anchored leader getpid with its actual PID, followed by its zero exit event, leader attachment observation, zero candidate status, and empty candidate stdout. Reject tracer errors, incomplete records and missing final newline.
cases.primary_evidence_gate: Primary must independently gate raw records; generic runner labels alone are not evidence. For each invocation reject as infrastructure/incomplete if setup status is nonzero or timed out; any diagnostic is missing, unreadable or truncated; setup-controls is malformed, incomplete, has an error, lacks invoked=true or candidate status/timeout, or does not establish the two distinct task IDs, shared gates [0,0,1,1], owner/tracer parentage, matching task IDs, and initial TracerPid=0; parser controls are missing/incomplete or a positive or negative control failed; native-control is incomplete, has an error or nonzero statuses, or its raw control/fixture outputs do not establish the expected calls, returns, both exits and both markers; either release, worker disappearance before leader release, fixture zero exit, fixture markers or clean fixture stderr is missing; or either candidate output reaches the capture limit. Assess only the files appropriate to a failed setup stage, retaining all available raw diagnostics; incomplete setup never supplies product evidence. After successful setup also reject missing/malformed/truncated assertions or classification infrastructure_error, wrong requirement or disagreement with independent parsing of raw candidate output and recorded identities. Neither zero tracer samples nor failure to attach is an infrastructure rejection: with successful fixture controls, classify those and complete malformed/error candidate output or candidate timeout as candidate mismatch. A match requires all case-specific complete ordered events, observed attachment and candidate status/output checks. These rules require a primary implementation and review; they do not change runner labels or claim GNU output equivalence.
